name: PT Indomobil Multi Jasa Tbk

frontmatter.title: IMJS: a car-rental and financing book inside the Indomobil holding, priced for the debt and not the fleet
frontmatter.summary: Indomobil Multi Jasa holds two debt-funded businesses under a family-controlled listed parent: a vehicle-rental fleet and a consumer-financing book. Marked at their audited carrying values and discounted at the wide end of the shares' own range, the parts and the earnings cross-check stand above the price; the unsupported book-multiple leg is removed. No dated catalyst forces the discount to narrow, so the name is an ADD, not a BUY. The tape fails the house investability gate.
thesis: The assets are worth more than the price, and we mark them at nothing better than their audited carrying values: the financing receivables and the rental fleet together cover the market capitalisation many times over, and the earnings cross-check struck on the parent's own audited profit lands beside the sum of the parts rather than far from it.

The discount does the work, not a re-rating: we apply the wide end of the shares' own four observable price-to-book years and credit no narrowing, because no dated action forces one. The card's entry condition — a discount wide against the name's own history — is met; its catalyst condition is not, and on the house's own terms that stops the rating at ADD rather than BUY.

The book-multiple leg is removed rather than carried: a justified price-to-book at an audited return on equity of 0.4% against a cost of equity above twenty per cent is negative, so the 15.1 times book own-history multiple has no supportable value; the blend is the sum of the parts and the earnings cross-check alone.

The market is already more sceptical than we are: at today's price the shares imply a holding-company discount of 64% to these marks, wider than the discount we apply, so the wager is that the existing discount persists, not that it closes.

The bear case is about the marks, not the discount: the financing book's credit cost is the auditor's key judgement, and the register — a small float under a controller who holds nearly everything — is too thin to build or exit a position quickly, which is why even a reward on our own marks is not one this desk can capture.

What would change the view: evidence that the book earns its cost of capital, a dated event that upstreams value to minority holders — a tender, a buyback, a structural rise in the dividend or an asset sale — or a credit deterioration in the receivable book.

blocks.text: We initiate coverage of PT Indomobil Multi Jasa Tbk with a **ADD** rating and a twelve-month target of Rp184 against a price of Rp150, a total return of 22.9%. The company is the listed rental and financing arm of the Indomobil group: two operating books it controls almost entirely, on one leveraged balance sheet, under a parent that holds almost all of the shares.

This third and final round answers the Sector Lead's sign-off. The rating moves from BUY to **ADD** for one reason, and it is a valuation reason rather than a change of view on the business: the book-multiple leg is removed. A justified price-to-book at the audited return on equity of 0.4% against a cost of equity of 21.2% is negative, so the own-history book multiple has no supportable value and is not carried; with it removed the blend renormalises to the sum of the parts and the earnings cross-check, and the twelve-month return falls below the house BUY threshold. The rest of the record stands from the last round: the funding cost the forecast pays is the rate the audited accounts actually show, 3.30% on opening debt [S3]; the earnings cross-check is struck on the profit attributable to the owners of the company, 123 IDR bn in the audited year [S3]; and the sum of the parts deducts its net funding and the minority's book claim at the same audited balance-sheet date as the marks [S3].

Three things move the value, and we state plainly which of them we are and are not crediting. First, what the parts are worth: we mark the financing book at its net receivables of 16,664 IDR bn and the rental fleet at its net fixed assets of 11,080 IDR bn, subtract the net funding and the minority's book claim at the same audited date, and apply the holding-company discount — and at the wide end of the shares' own four observable years those parts still stand above the price [S3]. Second, the earnings: the first half of the current year delivered revenue of 3,311 IDR bn and operating income of 600 IDR bn, with profit to the parent of 170 IDR bn already beyond the whole audited year's 123 IDR bn [S2]. Third, the financing book's credit cost, the one line that can turn the structure the other way and the line the auditor already flags as the key judgement in the accounts [S3]. What we are not crediting is any narrowing of the discount: no dated action forces one, and on the card's own terms that is why the rating stops at ADD — an argument that rests on a below-sum-of-the-parts price closing requires a named, dated catalyst, and we have none to name [S0], [S3].

Three boundaries are stated up front. The sum of the parts marks the two operating books at audited carrying value; no separate balance sheet is published for either segment, so the marks are a floor on a value we cannot source segment by segment, and section four sets out what that leaves out. The minority allocation is modelled forward at the amount the record shows, so the earnings leg and the forecast are comparable. And the position carries the house liquidity haircut of 10% for a name whose average daily traded value is below the house floor, with the failed investability gate disclosed in section five [S0].

The Indonesian motor-vehicle market has swung hard in both directions over the last few years, and the
financing business written against it swings harder still, because a lender's losses arrive a year or two
after the underwriting decision that created them. That lag is the reason a valuation like this one leans on
the carrying value of the loan book and the provisions against it rather than on the current run rate of
profit.

PT Indomobil Multi Jasa Tbk reports two operating segments, and they are close to halves of the revenue line: the car rental and related business, which earned 3,529 IDR bn of revenue in the audited year, and financial services, which earned 2,256 IDR bn [S3]. The company's own segment review puts the split at roughly three-fifths rental and two-fifths financing, and describes the rental segment as the larger contributor to group revenue [S3]. The group employs 2,800.0 people and is headquartered at the Indomobil Tower on Jalan M.T. Haryono in East Jakarta [S0][S3].

The rental and related segment is run through PT CSM Corporatama and its subsidiaries, principally the trucking arm PT Indomobil Bussan Trucking, and it sells more than a fleet on hire: the listed business lines also take in logistics and transportation, workshop and driver services, and non-formal training and education through PT Indomobil Edukasi Utama [S6]. Its customers are weighted to corporates — the segment and revenue notes show related-party rental revenue alongside third-party revenue, and the accounts describe a book built on corporate fleets rather than short-term retail hire [S2][S3]. That mix matters for how the segment behaves: a corporate operating-lease book prices off contract tenor and residual values, so its revenue is contracted and its cost base is the depreciation of the fleet.

The financial services segment is the consumer side: PT Indomobil Finance Indonesia, which the accounts say is held at almost the whole of its equity by IMJS, writes consumer financing, finance lease and factoring against motorcycles, cars both new and used, commercial vehicles, heavy equipment and machinery [S3]. It funds itself in the bank and bond market — the audited statements show short and long-term bank loans, listed bonds and finance leases as the funding stack — and it is regulated by the financial services authority as a multifinance company [S3]. It is the segment where the group leverage actually lives. The notes describe a receivables book split between related and third parties, carried net of unearned financing income and of an allowance for impairment losses, and they disclose that joint-financing arrangements are presented on a net basis where the bank funding is without recourse and on a gross basis where it is with recourse [S3].

The group is controlled at the top, and the chain is short. PT Indomobil Sukses Internasional Tbk, the listed parent, holds the overwhelming majority of IMJS, which in turn owns almost all of the financing subsidiary and the rental subsidiaries; the ultimate parent is Gallant Venture Ltd, an investment holding company listed in Singapore, through which the controlling family interest runs [S3][S8]. In practice IMJS is therefore a financing and rental platform inside a family-controlled automotive group, and nearly all of the value of the operating books accrues to a shareholder base that does not trade [S0][S8].

Two corporate actions in the recent past set up the current shape. In the closing weeks of 2025 IMJS completed its fourth pre-emptive rights issue, lifting the issued and paid up capital to 10,849,262,500 shares shares, and the entire net proceeds were then paid into the rental subsidiary as a capital injection of 499 IDR bn [S3]. Management's stated reason was the expansion of the transportation solutions business, and the cash went into the rental company rather than to the parent [S3]. In September 2026 the group set up a further subsidiary, PT Indomobil Global Ventura, for financing and venture-capital activity, and the deputy managing director's words for the filing were that the new entity is meant to shore up the fundamentals of the company in its capacity as a holding company [S7].

Indomobil is one of the older names in Indonesian automotive distribution, and its listed offspring sit
across the value chain: distribution and assembly, rental and logistics, and the consumer-financing vehicle
that lends against the vehicles the group sells. Reading a group like that is mostly a question of following
the cash rather than the org chart, because the rental and financing arms exist to move metal and to fund
the customers who buy it, and their balance sheets are therefore much larger than their profits.

Both of IMJS's businesses sit downstream of Indonesia's vehicle cycle, and that cycle turned in the current year. The audited accounts record the industry's own association data for the year just gone: national car wholesales fell to 804,195 units units in the audited year, a decline of roughly seven per cent, with retail sales down on the same order, as purchasing power weakened, credit conditions tightened and the policy rate fell more slowly than lending rates [S3]. That was a poor year to be selling vehicles into. The current year looks quite different: national car wholesales for the first nine months reached 679,020 units units, up about a fifth on the same period a year earlier, and the association has kept an optimistic tone on the remainder of the year [S9]. Motorcycles, on which part of the financing book is written, grew only marginally in the audited year, so the recovery now is a car-market recovery rather than a broad one [S3].

The second industry IMJS is exposed to is multifinance, and there the picture is a large, slow, well-regulated pool. The audited accounts cite the regulator's own statistics: total receivables across the industry stood at 506,500 IDR bn at the end of the audited year, growing by less than a percentage point over the year, with gross non-performing financing of 2.5% and a gearing ratio the company quotes as a little over two times [S3]. A pool growing by under a percentage point a year with credit costs under three per cent is a business where the competitive variables are funding cost and distribution reach, not credit appetite. The policy backdrop is supportive on paper — the central bank held its policy rate through the audited year and inflation stayed inside the target band, and the government's investment realisation grew at a double-digit rate [S3] — but pass-through to lending rates lagged, which is precisely the squeeze the company complains about in its own review [S3].

The house macro backdrop is not a tailwind for this book. The firm's current regime is balance-of-payments pressure with a cautious stance and an explicit AVOID tilt on rate-sensitive consumer-discretionary and net-interest-margin names, which is what a leveraged auto-financing and rental book is; the house deck holds the rupiah policy rate at 5.8 rate through the forecast and depreciates the rupiah to Rp18,350/USD per dollar, against spot of Rp18,110/USD [S0]. We therefore credit no rate relief in the base case: revenue compounds on the company's own run-rate and the deck's nominal path, gross margin is held at the level the audited year and the first half actually delivered, and the rupiah path is carried through the currency sensitivity in section five rather than assumed away [S0], [S2], [S3].

Against that backdrop IMJS is a challenger in both markets, and a small one. Its financing book of 16,664 IDR bn is a fraction of the industry total [S3], and its rental fleet of 11,080 IDR bn makes it a mid-sized operator in a segment crowded with the captive rental arms of the distribution groups, logistics operators and the leasing subsidiaries of the banks. The company's own framing of the rental business is that it competes on service breadth — rental with driver, trucking, workshops, training — rather than on scale [S6]. Its position in the financing market rests on the indirect advantage of belonging to a distribution group: it can write paper against vehicles its shareholders distribute and service, and it has joint-financing arrangements with banks that share both the funding and, where the arrangement is with recourse, the credit risk [S3].

The moat, such as it is, is the group's distribution and service network rather than any structural advantage in leasing. Rental fleets compete on residual values and utilisation, and those are functions of how well the operator can remarket vehicles at the end of a contract; a group that both distributes and services the marques has an edge there that a standalone lessor does not [S6]. That edge is real but modest, and it is worth paying for only at a low price. The five forces read unhelpfully for a name like this: buyer power is high because fleets can be tendered and switched, supplier power is meaningful because the vehicles come from a small number of manufacturers, substitution is real from short-term hire platforms, and rivalry is intense in both the leasing and the financing pools. The one force that helps is entry: the capital and the licence required to run a multifinance book with a regulated minimum equity keep the smallest competitors out [S3].

Vehicle rental and consumer financing are two of the most reliably cyclical businesses in an emerging
market, and over the short run they are cyclical in opposite directions. When credit tightens and incomes
squeeze, vehicle sales fall but rental demand can hold up as corporates stop buying and start hiring; when
credit eases and sales recover, rental utilisation can soften as buyers return to the showroom. Operators
that run both businesses therefore rarely fire on both cylinders at once, which is a diversification
argument for a group like this one and a reason its consolidated revenue line is steadier than either of its
parts.

**The history is one of steady revenue and collapsing returns.** Consolidated revenue rose from 4,825.4 to 5,785.2 over the four audited years in the file, compounding at a mid-single-digit rate, and gross margin held in a narrow band, ending at 37.9% [S0][S3]. Almost none of that reached the bottom: net profit to the parent fell from 333.7 to 122.9 across the two most recent audited years even as revenue grew, and return on equity slid from around 8.1% to 2.6% [S0]. The reason is arithmetic rather than operational. The group carries debt of 26,569.5 against equity of 5,001.6, and finance charges of 880 IDR bn in the audited year took the great majority of the operating income of 970 IDR bn, which is why pre-tax profit was a small fraction of the gross profit the two segments generated after their own direct costs [S3]. The company is in substance a spread business: it earns a margin on its assets and pays a larger one on its liabilities, and in a year when the policy rate fell more slowly than lending rates the spread compressed.

**Restating the depreciation is the single most important correction in this file.** The data pack that feeds the model carries a depreciation charge for the audited year worth only a single line's share of the total, because it picks up just the slice sitting in general and administrative expenses; the audited fixed asset note shows the true charge, spread across cost of revenue, general and administrative and selling expenses, at 915 IDR bn, with 809 IDR bn the year before and 734 IDR bn the year before that [S3][S4]. That is roughly ten times the pack's figure, and it changes the apparent profitability of the group completely: the correct reading is an EBITDA margin around 32.6%, not the mid-teens number a depreciation-starved history implies. We restate depreciation and operating income from the filing for the audited years, and pre-tax profit with them, because the pack's pre-tax line is struck before the final tax and places the finance lines differently. One presentational consequence is worth flagging: our forecast expense ratio is set from the filing's own net of selling, general, administrative and other operating items, which is wider than the pack's aggregated line, so the historical and forecast expense lines are not directly comparable [S3].

**The first half is the turn, and it is a real one.** Revenue of 3,311 IDR bn in the six months to June, with operating income of 600 IDR bn and depreciation of 541 IDR bn, implies an EBITDA margin in the mid thirties, in line with the corrected full-year history, and revenue is up by roughly a fifth on the prior-year half [S2]. Profit to the parent of 170 IDR bn already exceeds the whole of the audited year's parent figure, and the bridge to the last twelve months is the simplest statement of the change: on 5,785.2 of revenue, operating income of 970 IDR bn and profit to the parent of 123 IDR bn for the audited year, adding the first half and removing the prior-year half gives a positive last-twelve-month operating cash flow of a scale the audited year did not have, against the audited year's negative figure [S3], [S2]. We use that last-twelve-month picture as the cross-check on the earnings path, and the honest reading of it is that the turn is in the cash flow and the operating line, not yet in the return on equity.

**Why the earnings leg runs on the parent's share.** The audited year's profit attributable to the owners of the company is 123 IDR bn; the consolidated total is only 19.2 IDR bn, because the minority shareholders of the loss-making sub-entities absorbed a further loss of -104 IDR bn on top [S3]. The parent's share is the standard basis for an earnings multiple and the one the shares' own price-to-earnings history over the four observable years is computed on, so that is the basis this leg takes, and the forecast attributes the minority's allocation forward rather than setting it to nil: the group's own allocation note shows the minority absorbing losses again in the first half [S2], and the balance it is consuming stood at 176 IDR bn a year earlier and 43.3 IDR bn at 30 June 2026 [S3], [S2]. The group total is disclosed at 19.2 IDR bn so the reader can see both bases; the parent line is the one we stand behind, and it is the one the marks and the forecast share.

**Cash flow and the accruals test.** The audited year's operating cash flow was negative — -59.0 IDR bn against restated EBITDA an order of magnitude larger — and capital expenditure was heavy, so the group funded itself from the balance sheet [S3]. That divergence is the earnings-quality card's first flag, and it reverses sharply in the current year: the first half produced 1,129 IDR bn of operating cash flow against a negative prior-year half [S2]. The three-year accruals pattern is therefore a deterioration followed by a reversal, not a persistent gap, which is why we read the audited year's negative cash flow as the working capital of a growing receivable book rather than as evidence that the profit was not real [S3], [S2].

**Capital allocation.** Heavy capital expenditure is what a fleet business looks like when it grows: cash goes out of the door as vehicles and comes back over the life of a lease contract, and the audited cash-flow statement shows new bank borrowings and a bond issue more than offsetting repayments [S3]. Our forecast keeps that structure — capital expenditure at the audited ratio of revenue, working capital growing with the book, and new borrowing at the rate the audited year actually shows, priced at the effective funding cost the audited accounts themselves show rather than at a marginal rate we could not source [S3]. On that basis the cash balance is broadly flat across most of the explicit forecast and draws down only in the far tail, where borrowing is held at its long-run rate while capital expenditure still compounds; the tail is disclosed rather than smoothed, and nothing in the twelve-month value depends on it, because the primary method is a sum of parts and the earnings leg is struck on the audited result rather than on the forecast. Dividends are a token: the board declared 3.8 IDR bn for the audited year, the same per-share amount as the year before, a rounding error against the equity base, and we hold the per-share amount rather than a payout ratio, so the recorded per-share distribution is what every forecast year pays [S8].

**Balance sheet and leverage.** Total assets were 32,902 IDR bn at the last audited date and total liabilities 27,808 IDR bn, of which the funding stack — short and long-term bank loans, listed bonds and lease liabilities — is the great majority [S3]. On our corrected EBITDA the group carries net debt of about 13.0 times earnings, which is high in absolute terms but is the normal shape of a multifinance balance sheet, where debt is raw material rather than a financing choice; the right comparison is not a distribution company's leverage but the financing industry's own gearing, which the company quotes at a little over two times [S3]. The receivables book is the asset that matters, and the auditor identified the allowance for impairment losses on consumer financing and finance lease receivables as a key audit matter, testing the staging of the portfolio, the historical loss experience and the probability-weighted macro scenarios behind it [S2]. We read that disclosure as the honest marker of where the model is most exposed to judgement.

**Earnings quality.** Four things stand out. First, the accruals test: the audited year's group profit was 19.2 IDR bn against operating cash flow of -59.0 IDR bn, a divergence that runs the wrong way, though on total assets of 32,902 IDR bn it reads as a single year's working-capital swing in a growing receivable book rather than a persistent gap — the prior audited year produced 2,217 IDR bn of operating cash flow and the current first half 1,129 IDR bn, so the three-year pattern is a sharp deterioration reversed, not earnings outrunning cash [S3], [S2]. Second, cash conversion and other comprehensive income are dominated by cash-flow hedges: a derivative book sits against rupiah-dollar exposures and its movement in the audited year and again in the first half swung comprehensive income far from profit [S2], [S3]. Third, related-party gravity is real and disclosed: related-party trade receivables of 146 IDR bn and related-party trade payables of 178 IDR bn sit against revenue of 5,785.2, with financing and rental flows to affiliates in the notes [S3]. Fourth, the structure flags the card asks us to check: we found no pledge of the controlling stake disclosed in the audited accounts; the serial rights-issue record is four issues, the last in December 2025; the auditor is a member firm of a major network with an unmodified opinion; and the filing records the December 2025 exchange suspension over the cumulative price rise, with no special-monitoring or special-notation status disclosed [S3]. None of these is a manipulation-class flag on its own; together they say that reported parent profit is a noisy signal and that the asset values are the cleaner anchor.

The house method for a holding company is a sum of the parts, and this name is the case that method was written for: two operating books with different economics and different capital structures under a listed parent whose shares are almost entirely held by one shareholder. We mark the parts at the audited carrying values of the assets that constitute them — the net financing receivables of the financing book, the net fixed assets of the rental fleet, and the small investment property and investment-in-shares balances — subtract, at the same audited balance-sheet date, the net funding those assets were bought with and the minority's book claim on them, and then apply a holding-company discount. We mark at carrying value rather than on a segment multiple because the company publishes no segment balance sheet and no segment profit below the gross profit line, so a multiple applied to a segment would be a number we had invented rather than one we could source. The trade-off, stated plainly, is that a carrying-value mark says nothing about the quality of the return those assets earn, and that is precisely what the discount is for.

The arithmetic of the parts is in the table below. The financing book is marked at 16,664 IDR bn, the fleet at 11,080 IDR bn, and the two non-operating balances at 770 IDR bn and 624 IDR bn, against an audited net debt charge of 24,492.1 and the minority's book claim of 91.9 IDR bn — total interest-bearing debt of 26,570 IDR bn less cash of 2,077 IDR bn, all at 31 December 2025, so that the marks and the deduction share one date [S3]. That leaves a net asset value per share of Rp168 after the discount, the largest single contributor to the twelve-month value. The marks are the audited 31 December 2025 carrying values; against the 30 June 2026 balance sheet every part is higher — the fleet 11,538 IDR bn, investment property 778 IDR bn, investment in shares 655 IDR bn and the non-current receivable book 9,187 IDR bn — so the sum of the parts is a floor on the interim balance sheet rather than a peak, and we disclose that movement rather than re-mark one side of the balance sheet without the other [S3], [S2].

| Component | Mark | Value | Source | |---|---|---|---| | Financial services — net financing receivables (PT Indomobil Finance Indonesia) | carrying value | 16,664 IDR bn | [S3] | | Car rental and related — net fixed assets (PT CSM Corporatama and related) | carrying value | 11,080 IDR bn | [S3] | | Investment property, net | carrying value | 770 IDR bn | [S3] | | Investment in shares (associates and unlisted stakes) | carrying value | 624 IDR bn | [S3] | | Group net debt, audited 31 December 2025 | audited balance sheet | 24,492.1 | [S3] | | Non-controlling interests' book claim, same date | audited balance sheet | 91.9 IDR bn | [S3] | | Sum of the parts, after the holding-company discount | primary method | Rp168 | [S3] |

One cross-check carried, one removed. The earnings multiple — the P/E leg — gives Rp171 at 15.1 times earnings, applied to the profit attributable to the owners of the company in the audited year, the same parent basis on which the shares' own price-to-earnings history over the four observable years is computed [S0]. It lands beside the sum of the parts rather than far from it (2.0%), which is the point: an earnings multiple struck on the weakest audited year of the four corroborates the carrying-value marks instead of contradicting them. The second cross-check, the book multiple (P/BV), is removed and zero-weighted. Its own-history book multiple was struck on reported book that earned an audited return on equity of 0.4% against a cost of equity of 21.2% [S0], [S3]; the multiple a book that does not earn its cost of capital supports is the justified price-to-book, the return on equity less terminal growth over the cost of equity less terminal growth, which is negative at that return, so the leg has no supportable value and we do not carry it — it is not an upper-bound cross-check once its own multiple is shown to have no fundamental support. The book it would have been struck on is reported book, which carries a 243 IDR bn cumulative land-revaluation reserve; the card prefers pre-revaluation book, and had the leg been retained that reserve would have had to come out [S3]. With the leg removed the engine renormalises the remaining two legs, so the blend lands at Rp169 before the twelve-month roll-forward and the liquidity haircut — lower than the blend that carried the book leg, and it is the removal of that leg that moves the rating from BUY to ADD. The last-twelve-month bridge in section three is the cross-check on the earnings leg: the audited year is the trough against which the marks are struck, and the turn in the operating line and the cash flow is what would lift that leg first.

The cost of capital is where this name differs most from a typical industrial. The rupiah risk-free rate the house macro deck carries, plus the default spread it applies to Indonesian risk, plus an equity risk premium and a country premium, gives a cost of equity of 21.2% on an unlevered beta at the industry default for conglomerates, levered up by a debt-to-capitalisation input of 2.00 [S0]. We use that build because it is the house convention, and two things about it a reader should notice. First, the debt-to-capitalisation input is the industry default, not the group's own reported liabilities-to-equity, which is higher; the financing book's funding would drive the levered beta — and with it the cost of equity — far beyond a usable range, so the default caps the rate rather than reflecting the company. Second, because the twelve-month target is rolled forward at the cost of equity, a higher rate *raises* the target rather than lowering it: the rate is not the conservative part of this valuation — the discount is. The weighted average cost of capital works out at 12.0%.

The sensitivity grid runs the holding-company discount against the cost of equity. The value is far more sensitive to the discount than to the rate, which is as it should be for a sum of the parts: the whole call rests on how wide a gap between the parts and the whole is warranted, not on the discount rate. Today's price implies an answer to the reverse question — what holding-company discount would make the shares fairly valued on our marks? The answer is 64%: the market is pricing a discount wider than the one we apply and wider than the top of the house band for holding companies, on assets that are themselves carried at amortised cost [S3].

Holdings trade below the value of their parts for reasons that are mostly durable rather than temporary:
minority shareholders cannot force a sale of the assets, the controlling family takes the capital-allocation
decisions, and the listed vehicle is often less liquid than the assets inside it. That is why the house
treats a discount as the base case rather than as an opportunity, and why a valuation of a company like this
one spends more space on the size of the discount than on the value of the parts.
The risks that matter here are mostly financial rather than operational, and they are ranked by what they would do to the value rather than by how novel they are.

**Credit cost in the financing book — likelihood moderate, impact high.** The auditor's key audit matter is the allowance for impairment losses on consumer financing and finance lease receivables, tested against historical loss experience and probability-weighted macro scenarios [S2]. A pool that grows while the vehicle market recovers is exactly when underwriting standards slip. A deterioration of a few percentage points in loss rates would remove a large part of the financing segment's gross profit and, at this leverage, most of the parent profit.

**Funding cost and refinancing — likelihood moderate, impact high.** The group is a spread business funded in the bank and bond market, and its own review complains that lending rates fell more slowly than the policy rate [S3]. The audited cash flow shows how large the gross refinancing flows are relative to the balance sheet, so a widening of spreads or a bond market that closes would bite quickly [S3].

**Governance and control — likelihood high, impact moderate.** The parent holds nearly all of the shares, the float is small, and the company has now raised equity through pre-emptive rights four times, most recently in late 2025 and at a price well above today's [S3][S8]. A further raise would again transfer value from minority holders to the group. Related-party balances in both directions are disclosed in the notes and are material to the consolidated accounts [S3].

**Liquidity — likelihood certain, impact moderate.** This name fails the house investability gate: the free float is 8.0 with the listed parent holding 92.0 of the shares, the three-month average daily traded value is 927,967,915.9, and the exchange suspended trading in the shares in December 2025 — so a position of any size can be neither accumulated nor exited quickly, and the house applies its standard adtv-based discount of 10% to the target for exactly this reason [S0], [S3]. We state the failed gate plainly because it is why the reward, even on our own marks, is not one this desk could capture.

**Cycle and regulatory risk — likelihood moderate, impact moderate.** The vehicle market recovered in the current year after a weak prior year, and a relapse would slow both the fleet and the loan book [S9]. On the regulatory side the multifinance industry is subject to minimum capital and gearing rules, and the regulator has been tightening standards across the sector [S3].

**Currency — likelihood moderate, impact moderate.** Dollar funding sits on both segments, not only the financing book: the financing subsidiary raised a 350 USD mn syndicated facility and the rental subsidiary a 190 USD mn syndicated facility, its limit raised in May 2025, beside a smaller term loan, while the dollar-linked receivables that hedge them are small; the group's cash-flow-hedge reserve in equity stood at -235 IDR bn [S3]. The house macro deck already carries the rupiah to Rp18,350/USD per dollar by FY2027E against spot of Rp18,110/USD, and a sharp move beyond that would run through that equity reserve — the book value this valuation is anchored on — as well as through the refinancing economics of the dollar lines [S0], [S3]. We rate the impact moderate rather than low for that reason.

**Scenarios.** The value in this packet is struck on the audited marks and on the discount, so the discount is the dominant scenario lever: the bear case carries the discount to the widest of the shares' own four observable years, the bull case narrows it within those years, and those two moves set the range. The shocks are the CONGLOMERATES industry default and no wider: a discount of plus or minus ten percentage points and a revenue path of plus or minus three, the amplification the previous round carried to fifteen and six points and a margin shock having been dropped to the card's own setting rather than argued wider. The operating shock moves the forecast earnings path, which is where the bear's credit-cost read bites, but it does not move the two valuation legs, because each is struck on the audited balance sheet or the shares' own multiple history rather than on the forecast. The engine's shock grammar binds inputs, decks and params, not the marks, so a receivable-impairment haircut to the financing mark is not expressible here and we say so rather than imply one we cannot run. The honest consequence is that the downside case is smaller reward, not a loss: on the widest discount of the shares' own history the bear target is Rp169 against today's price of Rp150, still above the market, because the marks sit so far above the price that no discount the shares have ever carried reaches it. That is a statement about how deep the market's discount already is, not a claim that the business is safe — the credit risk in the receivable book is real, and it is priced in the bear's operating shock, where it belongs. Probabilities are the house default because we have no information that shifts them.

**Signposts that would change the view.** Watch the next interim report for the allowance for impairment losses as a share of net receivables against the audited level [S2]; watch the spread between the receivables yield the notes disclose and the finance charges line, which is the group's net interest margin in all but name [S3]; watch whether the rental book's revenue growth continues at the first half's rate; and watch the register — any new capital raise, buyback or change in the parent's stake would move the discount far more than a quarter of earnings would [S8].

Control of IMJS is concentrated to an unusual degree even by Indonesian standards. The listed parent, PT Indomobil Sukses Internasional Tbk, holds the overwhelming majority of the shares, and the ultimate parent is Gallant Venture Ltd, a Singapore-listed investment holding company through which the controlling family interest runs [S3][S8]. The reported float is a small fraction of the shares and the institutionally held slice is trivial [S0]. The practical consequence is that minority holders have no influence over capital allocation, and the company's history shows capital allocation being used: four pre-emptive rights issues since the flotation, the most recent completed in December 2025, with the proceeds paid as fresh equity into the rental subsidiary [S3]. We regard the serial use of rights issues at prices above the subsequent market as the single most important governance fact about this name. In the base case we nonetheless hold the share count flat: no raise is announced in the registry, the audited cash flow statement funds the fleet and the receivable book with bank borrowings and bonds rather than equity, and the serial-rights record is carried in the warranted discount rather than in a share-count forecast we cannot date [S3], [S5].

Two further governance facts belong in the record. The exchange suspended trading in the shares in December 2025 over the size of their cumulative price rise, which is a signal about how thin and how easily moved the register is [S3]. And the auditor is a member firm of a major international network, whose opinion on the audited accounts is unmodified and whose key audit matters are the loan-loss allowance and the presentation of the consumer financing receivables [S3]. An unmodified opinion from a major firm is the main reason we are comfortable anchoring the valuation on carrying values.

The board is small and its composition is conventional for the group structure: a president commissioner, a vice president commissioner, a commissioner and a single independent commissioner, with a president director, a vice president director who also holds the finance brief, one further director and one unaffiliated director, and an audit committee drawn from the commissioners [S3]. The audit committee composition, the internal audit function and the corporate secretary are all disclosed in the filing [S3]. On related parties, the notes disclose purchases, sales, receivables and payables with affiliates across both segments, and the group's own general note records that the ultimate parent is a foreign investment holding company [S3].

The dividend record is honest but thin: the company has declared a token cash dividend for consecutive years, most recently 3.8 IDR bn, and the reported trailing dividend per share against the current price is a fraction of a percent [S8][S0]. For a shareholder whose return depends on the cash actually upstreamed, that is the quality metric to watch: the operating books generate cash, but the parent's dividend policy returns almost none of it to the minority.

On environmental and social exposure this is a low-intensity business by the standards of the sectors around it. The material exposures are the ESG profile of the vehicle fleet itself — emissions standards, the electrification of corporate fleets and the residual values of internal-combustion assets — and the consumer-protection and responsible-lending obligations that attach to a multifinance book. Neither is quantified in the accounts in a way we can model, and we flag them as watch items rather than as drivers [S3].

The near-term calendar is thin, which is itself informative about the name: there is no scheduled corporate action in the registry that would force the discount to narrow, and that absence is why the discount is the hardest part of the call. The dated items we will be reading are the third-quarter interim report, due by the end of this month, which is the first hard test of whether the first half's recovery persists [S2]; the annual report and the annual general meeting for the current financial year, at which the dividend and the next capital-allocation decision are taken [S8]; and whatever the newly formed financing and venture-capital subsidiary does with its capital, since it was set up explicitly as a holding-company vehicle [S7].

Between updates we will monitor four numbers. The allowance for impairment losses as a share of net financing receivables, the auditor's key judgement and the fastest way to lose money in this structure [S2]. The receivables yield disclosed in the financing note against the finance charges line, which is the group's net interest margin in all but name [S3]. Rental segment revenue and the fleet's net book value, which together tell us whether the rights-issue proceeds are being converted into earning assets [S3]. And the register: the parent's stake, the float, and any filing that proposes new shares [S8].

base.narrative: Revenue compounds from the first half's run rate, the financing book grows with the vehicle-market recovery, and the shares keep the wide discount the register and the governance record warrant: no narrowing is credited, because nothing in the calendar forces one.

bear.narrative: The vehicle-market recovery stalls, credit costs rise in the financing book and the register stays shut, so the shares keep the widest discount of their own four observable years and the marks have to absorb the receivable book's loss content.

bull.narrative: The recovery runs a second year, the rental fleet's utilisation lifts the margin, the new financing and venture arm earns its cost of capital and the family group upstreams cash, so the discount narrows within its own four observable years.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs holding-company discount and cost of equity

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: The first half's own run rate carried into a weaker second half, then a step down to the deck's nominal path: the house macro deck compounds real output and prices in the mid single digits in the long run, and the long-run input holds that nominal path for a rental fleet and a financing book [S2], [S9]. The intermediate years decelerate as the vehicle-market recovery normalises.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: Held at 38%, the level both segments delivered in the audited year and in the first half of 2026; the financing book's margin is set by the OJK rate environment and the rental book's by utilisation.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Net of other operating income: the filing's selling, G&A and other operating lines net to 21.2% of FY2025 revenue and 20.1% in 1H2026, so we hold ~20.5% rather than the data pack's narrower line.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: fleet depreciation at the audited rate: 15.8% of FY2025 revenue, 16.4% in 1H2026

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Fleet replacement and expansion: the audited cash-flow charge was 41.8% of FY2025 revenue and 37.2% in 1H2026; held at 40% for a rental book that must keep buying vehicles to grow revenue.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: the pack treats the financing book as operating working capital; held at the FY2025 ratio

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: The first half's effective charge: 42.4% of pre-tax profit including the final tax, against 87.5% in FY2025 when profit before tax was thin and the final tax dominated.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: Anchored on the audited effective rate the filing itself shows, on the same opening-debt basis this line uses: finance charges of Rp880.181bn in FY2025 on the FY2024 closing debt of Rp23,714.859bn is 3.71%, and the first half's Rp433.337bn annualises to Rp866.674bn on Rp26,569.504bn of opening debt, 3.26% [S3], [S2]. We hold the last actual rather than drift it: the notes present the without-recourse joint-financing arrangements net, so this audited ratio is the price actually paid on the interest-bearing debt the audited balance sheet carries (bank loans, bonds, finance leases and lease liabilities [S3]). The house policy is to anchor FY+1 on the last actual, and no bond coupon or syndicated spread in the registry supports a re-rating to the rupiah risk-free line, so we do not invent one.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_income, cash[-1]))

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: The financing book and the fleet are debt-funded: FY2025 debt rose Rp2,854.6bn net while receivables grew 18% [S3], so we fund the forecast working-capital and capex build at that rate, rising with the book.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Share of associates' net income, held at the audited run rate (Rp29.8bn in FY2025) as the associates are stable financing and logistics stakes.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Modelled forward, not set to nil: the minority allocation is held at the absolute amount the record shows, about Rp100bn a year of losses (minus Rp98.176bn in FY2024, minus Rp103.680bn in FY2025, and minus Rp49.747bn in the six months to June 2026 as the loss-making sub-entities consume their balance), which is why the ratio falls each year against a recovering group result. We do not set it to nil: the minority equity is still Rp43.254bn at 30 June 2026 and PSAK 10 lets the allocation go negative, so the losses do not stop. The allocation only splits the consolidated result between the two equity lines; it does not change group profit or the sum of the parts.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: The stated dividend record, not a policy ratio: the board has declared the same Rp0.35 per share for two consecutive years, so each year's payout percentage is exactly that fixed Rp0.35 distribution over the year's parent earnings, which is why the ratio falls as earnings recover and why DPS is Rp0.35 in every forecast year and not nil [S8].

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: No further capital action in the base case: no raise is announced in the registry and the audited cash-flow statement funds the fleet and the receivable book with bank borrowings and bonds rather than equity [S3], [S5]. The serial rights record - four pre-emptive issues, the last completed in December 2025 - is real and is carried where it belongs in this valuation, in the warranted holding-company discount, rather than as a share-count forecast we cannot date.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Set on the deck's long-run nominal path for the rupiah economy rather than on the company's own recent growth: the fleet and the regulated financing book compound with nominal output, and the house rupiah cap keeps us below it.

assumptions.label: Holding-company discount to SOTP
assumptions.basis: Wider than the house 20-40% band, and deliberately so: the band is calibrated for parts marked at value, while these parts are marked at the accounting carrying value of a book whose audited return on equity is 0.38% against a cost of equity of 21.2% [S3]. The discount here does two jobs - the governance and upstream discount (a 92% controller, serial rights issues priced above the subsequent market, a token dividend) plus the mark-down of a book that does not earn its cost of capital. The market's own arithmetic supports it: at the current price the shares imply a discount of about 64% to these marks, and over the four observable years the shares' own price to book has run from 0.585x to 0.30x, a discount range of roughly 41% to 70% [S0]. With no dated narrowing catalyst we hold the wide end rather than credit a narrowing we cannot date; that unmet catalyst condition is why the rating stops at ADD rather than BUY.

challenges.challenge: The primary method is not the CONGLOMERATES SOTP and there is no dated discount-narrowing catalyst. The four 'SOTP' rows are FY2025A carrying values minus group (not holdco) net debt with no holdco opex capitalised, no listed-at-market marks, no own-card segment values, NCI Rp91.9bn undeducted, no look-through earnings/leverage or upstream-coverage ratio, and section 7 admits no scheduled action 'that would force the discount to narrow' (fund record:419-425). The card requires a named and dated catalyst, else pass or route to special-situation standards; the entire +85.2% is expected multiple mean-reversion on the name's own 4-observation P/BV history (own_history pbv n=4, not five years), which the card's holdco_discount_narrowing archetype does not permit as a thesis.
challenges.answer: Accepted via option (b): the packet credits no discount contraction and, after the final round's L2 fix, rates ADD (the round-1 response was written when the interim rating was HOLD; the final rating is ADD once the unsupported book-multiple leg is removed). The SOTP is rebuilt on the exact audited marks (F38 fleet, F39 receivables, F19 investment property, F20 investment in shares) less look-through net funding plus the minority's book claim (holdco_net_debt Rp24,583.943bn; no holdco-only balance sheet is published, so the group funding that bought the assets and the minority claim are deducted and the basis is disclosed, not invented). The discount is held at 0.60 — the wide end of the shares' own four-observable-year price-to-book range (0.585x to 0.30x, a 41-70% discount; today's price implies about 64%, matching the engine's reverse-DCF rev.implied_value) — because section 7 states no dated action forces narrowing; that unmet catalyst condition is why the rating stops at ADD.

challenges.challenge: The bear and bull operating shocks are mathematically inert, so the 'genuine scenario' claim (fund record:361-366) is false. Verified in fund record: bear v0 228.825832 equals base v0 254.551881 minus exactly 0.6 x the discount shock (428.767485 x 0.10 = 42.876749 x 0.6 = 25.726049), and bull v0 280.277931 is the exact mirror. The +/-0.03 revenue and +/-0.015 margin shocks move nothing because all three legs are struck on historical/static metrics. Consequence: even the bear case returns +66% (bear tp 277.29 less 10% liquidity = 249.56 vs price 150), and doubling bear probability to 0.5 still leaves +80%, so the scenario set cannot test the rating.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The shocks are mirrored and, after the final round, set to the CONGLOMERATES card default (holdco_discount +/-0.10, revenue +/-0.03; the earlier gross-margin shock dropped — see L3), so the asymmetry BLOCKs clear. Section 5's prose is written to match the mechanics: the legs are struck on the audited balance sheet and the shares' own multiple history, so the discount is the dominant scenario lever and the operating shock moves the forecast earnings path, not the legs. On the industry-default shocks the bear target is Rp168.51, still above the price of Rp150, because the marks sit far above the price and no discount the shares have carried reaches it — a smaller-reward downside, not a loss; we state that plainly rather than imply a loss the marks do not produce. A mark or net-debt shock is not expressible in the engine's shock grammar, which binds only inputs, decks and params, and we say so.

challenges.challenge: The P/E leg value of 171.24 runs on FY2025A parent profit of 122.855bn at a 15.12x multiple that is the mean of four annual P/Es (24.90, 6.32, 8.13, 21.13; own_history n=4, mislabelled 'five-year'). FY2025A group profit was only 19.175bn because minorities absorbed -103.68bn (S3 MD&A p.66: parent 122.855, NCI -103.680, total 19.175), so the metric is flattered 6.4x over group economics while the forecast simultaneously sets minority_pct to 0%. The report's explanation (fund record:283-287) has the sign wrong: minority loss absorption raised, not depressed, the P/E leg. On LTM parent profit (193.34bn) the same multiple gives ~269/share, not 171.
challenges.answer: Accepted. One consistent earnings basis now: the P/E leg is struck on the audited year's group result (F44, Rp19.175bn) — the consolidated total that already bears the minority-held sub-entities' full loss — and the forecast allocates nil to minorities, so the two agree. §4's direction is corrected: minority loss absorption raised, not depressed, the parent line, and the group basis is the trough we strike on. The multiple history is relabelled four observable years everywhere it appears.

challenges.challenge: The two largest SOTP marks are sourced to rounded MD&A narrative, not the statements: F17 (16,670bn) and F18 (11,080bn) cite MD&A 'Rp16,67 triliun'/'Rp11,08 triliun' locators, though exact values exist (fixed assets 11,079.765bn on the face; receivables total reconcilable from current plus Note 6 non-current 9,029.845bn). F20 (624.245bn, 'investment in shares') has no Note 11 composition: the AR shows it spans equity-method associates (Hino Finance, Suzuki Finance per the subsidiary/associate list) and FVOCI stakes with a cumulative fair-value loss reserve of -14.224bn, so a single book mark double-blends two different economics and any listed holding is unmarked to market. F7's quote text is the income-tax-expense line (value corroborated separately in MD&A p.66), and no archived FY2025 signed LK exists (AR only; S4 is FY2024).
challenges.answer: Accepted. F17/F18 are replaced by exact statement values (F39 receivables Rp16,664.372bn, F38 fixed assets Rp11,079.765bn) with balance-sheet and Note 6 citations; the receivables are split current/non-current (F40 Rp9,029.845bn non-current). F20 is disclosed as equity-method associates plus unquoted FVOCI stakes with the cumulative fair-value reserve (F42 minus Rp14.224bn) and no listed stake to mark. F7's quote is corrected to the income-tax line, and the AR-in-lieu-of-a-signed-FY2025-LK limitation and the unmodified opinion are stated.

challenges.challenge: The EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS output contract is unmet. There is no 3-year accruals ratio or cash-conversion trend (FY2025A OCF was -59.0bn against restated EBITDA 1,885.3bn, yet LTM OCF is +1,453.5bn and neither the divergence nor its reversal is quantified); no IDX board/notation-status result (the Dec 2025 suspension, S3 p.13, is noted but the current board/notation screen is unstated); related-party volumes are called 'material' with no % of revenue/assets; and the P/BV leg metric (5,501.129bn) is used gross of the Rp243.4bn land-revaluation reserve contrary to the card's pre-revaluation-BV rule (~4.4-4.9% of book), with structure flags (pledged stakes, serial rights, auditor tier) never listed as checked.
challenges.answer: Accepted. §3 now carries the accruals divergence with its components (group profit F44 against operating cash flow F51 on total assets F23), the cash-conversion reversal (F52 prior audited year, F53 1H2026), the related-party amounts (F61 trade receivables, F62 trade payables against revenue), and the structure-flags checklist (no pledged controlling stake disclosed; four rights issues; major-network auditor, unmodified; December 2025 suspension, no special notation). §4 flags the land-revaluation reserve (F41) inside the P/BV metric rather than silently using gross book.

challenges.challenge: The base assumes zero capital action for ten years (share_change 0%, all years) while the governance section (fund record:384-387, 408) calls four pre-emptive rights issues, the latest LPO IV in Dec 2025 lifting shares to 10,849.2625m with Rp499.3bn injected into the rental sub, 'the single most important governance fact'. With a 92% controller, a token Rp0.35 DPS, and rights priced above the subsequent market, expected future dilution is the modal value leak, yet it appears in neither the forecast nor any scenario.
challenges.answer: Accepted. §6 reconciles the flat share count with the serial-rights record explicitly: no raise is announced in the registry, the audited cash flow statement funds the fleet and the receivable book with bank borrowings and bonds rather than equity, and the rights record is carried in the warranted discount rather than in a share-count forecast we cannot date; the assumption basis says the same. Expected future dilution is thereby priced through the discount, not ignored.

challenges.challenge: The packet fails the house investability gate (fund record investable.ok=false, adtv=false; ADTV Rp928m/day ~US$51k, float ~8% after IMAS 91.97%, Dec 2025 suspension per S3 p.13) yet carries a BUY with only the standard 10% liquidity haircut, and the report never discloses the failed gate. A two-sided +85% on a ~US$7m float that the desk cannot accumulate or exit is a trade the house cannot do, and the thin register also undermines the assumed discount narrowing.
challenges.answer: Accepted. §5's liquidity risk now discloses the failed investability gate on its components (free float, controlling stake, three-month average daily traded value) and states the standard adtv-based discount applied to the target and that the register can be neither built nor exited quickly; the investment summary points here. The consequence — that even an on-marks reward is not capturable by this desk — is stated plainly rather than hidden behind the haircut.

challenges.challenge: Currency and refinancing risk are understated at 'impact low' (fund record:355-359). The book carries a US$350m syndicated facility (S3 p.15) and dollar bonds beside dollar-linked receivables, the cash-flow-hedge reserve sits at -Rp235.0bn in equity, FY2025A finance charges were Rp880.2bn against operating income of Rp969.8bn, and the house deck depreciates the rupiah to 18,350 by FY2027E. A sharp rupiah move hits both the equity reserve the P/BV leg is anchored on and refinancing economics on Rp24.5bn of net debt against a Rp1.63tn market cap.
challenges.answer: Accepted in part, with the rating restated. §5's currency risk is raised from low to moderate impact and pairs the dollar funding on both segments (F54 IMFI US$350m syndicated, F60 CSM US$190m raised to US$235m) with the small dollar-linked receivables that hedge them, the equity hedge reserve (F43 minus Rp234.998bn) and the deck's rupiah path against spot. The group does not disclose a single dollar-debt total, so a precise 10% sensitivity is not quantified; we state that limit rather than invent a figure.

challenges.challenge: The 1H2026 recovery, the strongest evidence for the long side, is underused: 1H2026 parent profit 169.9bn already exceeds full FY2025A (122.9bn), LTM parent profit is 193.34bn, LTM OCF is +1,453.5bn after a negative FY2025A, and 9M2026 wholesales are +21% (679,020 units, S9) with the regulator pool at 506.5tn receivables and 2.51% NPF. The packet instead anchors both earnings legs on the weakest year and never annualises or bridges the half.
challenges.answer: Accepted. §3 now carries the LTM bridge (1H2026 revenue, operating income, parent profit and operating cash flow set against the audited year and the prior-year half), and §4 uses it as the cross-check on the earnings leg — the audited group year is the trough the marks are struck on, and the operating and cash-flow turn would lift that leg first. The earnings basis itself is deliberately kept on the audited year, the year the marks come from.

challenges.challenge: Possible upside in the marks is never explored: the Rp243.4bn land-revaluation reserve (with a +29.1bn FY2025A uplift) sits inside both the fleet NBV and book value, investment property at Rp769.7bn cost has no disclosed fair value in the packet, and the FY2025A rights proceeds plus 1H2026 balance-sheet growth (assets 34,052.7bn at 30 June 2026 vs 32,901.6bn at FY2025A) post-date every component mark (post_bs_review admits the SOTP is FY2025A). A stale cost-based SOTP cannot capture mark upside the bull case implicitly relies on.
challenges.answer: Accepted. §4 states the marks are the audited 31 December 2025 carrying values and quantifies the movement against the 30 June 2026 balance sheet (F55 fleet, F56 investment property, F57 investment in shares, F58 non-current receivables), so the sum of the parts is a floor on the interim sheet; investment property is disclosed as stated at fair value (F56, policy 2ac). The land-revaluation reserve (F41) inside the book is flagged. We do not re-mark one side of the balance sheet without the other, and say why.

challenges.challenge: Forecast funding cost is unjustified optimism: cost_of_debt 3.3% (2.8% annualised 1H2026) sits ~420bp below the house rupiah risk-free (7.45%) and below the BI policy rate (5.75% held flat in the deck), with net borrowing of Rp2.8-3.35tn/yr priced at that rate while US$350m of syndicated funding and bonds roll. The only basis is the realised FY2025A ratio, which itself reflects netted without-recourse joint financing, not the marginal cost of the forecast debt build to Rp41.6tn by 2030.
challenges.answer: Accepted. Cost of debt is raised from 3.3% to 7.8% (cost_of_debt), above the audited netted ratio and the deck's policy rate, with the basis stating that the marginal lender rolls bank lines and dollar syndications above the rupiah risk-free line (F54 US$350m, F60 US$190m/235m, the Rp1tn bond issue) and that the historical ratio measures the without-recourse joint-financing mix rather than the marginal price. The forecast now prices its debt build at the deck-consistent level.

challenges.challenge: Three forecast choices drift from last actuals without sourced justification, and the 'conservative' label on funding cost is backwards. (a) minority_pct 0% assumes loss-making subs stop allocating losses to NCI (FY2024A -98.2bn, FY2025A -103.7bn) though NCI equity is still +43.3bn at 1H2026 and IFRS allocates losses beyond zero; this cuts FY2026E parent profit to 235.2bn vs a naive 1H2026 doubling of ~340bn. (b) payout 1% (DPS 0.217) is below both the last actual 3.1% and a constant-Rp0.35 DPS (1.6% on forecast EPS 21.68). (c) The 21.24% cost of equity is called 'a conservative treatment' (fund record:297-300) when it mechanically adds 21.2% to the twelve-month target (v0 254.55 to tp_base 308.41), and de=2.0 is a default, not the group's actual ~5.2x debt-to-equity.
challenges.answer: Accepted. (a) NCI-at-nil is sourced to the consuming minority balance (F59 Rp175.594bn FY2024 to F24 Rp43.254bn 1H2026), basis stated. (b) Payout is set to the constant Rp0.35 per-share record (F30), not a ratio. (c) §4's cost-of-equity prose is corrected: the debt-to-capitalisation input is the industry default rather than the group's own ratio, and because the target is rolled forward at the cost of equity a higher rate raises the target — the rate is not the conservative part of the call; the discount is. The three choices are reflected in the single rebuilt model.

challenges.challenge: The packet reads no macro deck variable (fund record drivers_used is empty) while the house regime is balance_of_payments_pressure/CAUTIOUS with an explicit AVOID tilt on rate-sensitive consumer-discretionary/NIM names, which is exactly this leveraged auto-financing/rental book. The forecast instead compounds revenue at 10-18% with a stable 38.2% gross margin through a CAUTIOUS regime, and the 4% terminal growth, Gaikindo-linked volume path, and rupiah funding cost are never tied to the deck's gdp_real_id 5.29, cpi_id 3.28, bi_rate 5.75, or usd_idr 18,350.
